scenes.dialogue: Police have filed a charge sheet. Must the accused now face a full trial? Not automatically.
The court must first examine whether the legal threshold for proceeding is met.
Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or B N S S, discharge and framing of charges serve this screening function.
scenes.shown: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or BNSS, discharge and framing of charges serve this screening function.

scenes.dialogue: Discharge means the court finds that proceeding against the accused is not justified at this stage.
It differs from bail, which concerns liberty while the case continues. And it differs from an acquittal after trial.
Discharge requires judicial consideration and reasons. It does not happen merely because the accused denies the allegation.
Filing an application does not achieve it either. So first identify the court and the type of case.
Take an ordinary Sessions case committed under Section Two Thirty Two.
scenes.shown: Take an ordinary Sessions case committed under Section 232.

scenes.dialogue: Section Two Fifty lets the accused apply for discharge within sixty days from commitment.
scenes.shown: Section 250 lets the accused apply for discharge within 60 days from commitment.

scenes.dialogue: The Judge considers the record and documents, and hears the accused and the prosecution.
If there is not sufficient ground for proceeding, the Judge must discharge the accused and record reasons.
If there is ground for presuming an offence exclusively triable by the Sessions Court, Section Two Fifty One requires a written charge.
scenes.shown: If there is ground for presuming an offence exclusively triable by the Sessions Court, Section 251 requires a written charge.

scenes.dialogue: It must be framed within sixty days from the first hearing on charge. These are different starting points.
scenes.shown: It must be framed within 60 days from the first hearing on charge. These are different starting points.

scenes.dialogue: Some High Courts treat the sixty day application window as directory. Even so, apply within it.
scenes.shown: Some High Courts treat the 60-day application window as directory. Even so, apply within it.

scenes.dialogue: For a warrant case before a Magistrate instituted on a police report, Section Two Sixty Two applies.
scenes.shown: For a warrant case before a Magistrate instituted on a police report, Section 262 applies.

scenes.dialogue: Here, the accused may seek discharge within sixty days from supply of document copies under Section Two Thirty.
scenes.shown: Here, the accused may seek discharge within 60 days from supply of document copies under Section 230.

scenes.dialogue: The Magistrate considers the police report and papers, and hears both sides. If the charge is groundless, discharge with reasons follows.
If the test for proceeding is met, Section Two Sixty Three requires a written charge within sixty days from the first hearing on charge.
scenes.shown: If the test for proceeding is met, Section 263 requires a written charge within 60 days from the first hearing on charge.

scenes.dialogue: So here, the discharge clock starts from document supply, not commitment.
Take three dates. A Sessions case is committed on the first of June: that starts its discharge application period.
scenes.shown: Take three dates. A Sessions case is committed on 1 June: that starts its discharge application period.

scenes.dialogue: In a different Magistrate's police report warrant case, copies are supplied on the tenth of June: that starts its application period.
scenes.shown: In a different Magistrate's police-report warrant case, copies are supplied on 10 June: that starts its application period.

scenes.dialogue: If the first hearing on charge is on the first of July, the charge framing period runs from that hearing.
scenes.shown: If the first hearing on charge is on 1 July, the charge-framing period runs from that hearing.

scenes.dialogue: Record the correct event, instead of using one date for every deadline.
A charge is the court's formal statement of the offence the accused must answer.
Sections Two Thirty Four and Two Thirty Five cover its contents: the offence, the law, the time, the place and the person involved.
scenes.shown: Sections 234 and 235 cover its contents: the offence, the law, the time, the place and the person involved.

scenes.dialogue: Under Sections Two Fifty One and Two Sixty Three, the charge is read and explained, and the accused is asked about the plea.
scenes.shown: Under Sections 251 and 263, the charge is read and explained, and the accused is asked about the plea.

scenes.dialogue: If contested, the case moves into evidence. Framing charges does not establish guilt; the prosecution must prove its case.
At this stage, the court examines whether the material supplies a legally sufficient basis to proceed.
Strong suspicion founded on the material can justify framing charges. Proof beyond reasonable doubt belongs to the decision on guilt.
The court must apply its mind, but it should not conduct a mini trial by deciding which witness is truthful.
Equally, a bare accusation without the required legal ingredients is not enough.
The Supreme Court has repeatedly distinguished this screening from deciding guilt.
Suppose Arjun is accused of stealing Ravi's laptop, worth sixty thousand rupees.
scenes.shown: Suppose Arjun is accused of stealing Ravi's laptop, worth ₹60,000.

scenes.dialogue: Imagine the prosecution papers, even accepted at face value, contain nothing connecting Arjun to the theft.
His lawyer can then argue that the charge is groundless, and seek discharge. But suppose a witness account and supporting material link him to taking it.
Then a dispute about the witness's reliability may require evidence at trial.
The actual record controls the result; neither example guarantees an outcome.
Now, do not apply these sixty day timelines to every kind of case.
scenes.shown: Now, do not apply these 60-day timelines to every kind of case.

scenes.dialogue: Warrant cases instituted otherwise than on a police report follow Sections Two Sixty Seven to Two Sixty Nine.
scenes.shown: Warrant cases instituted otherwise than on a police report follow Sections 267 to 269.

scenes.dialogue: In summons cases, Section Two Seventy Four generally requires the accusation to be stated without a formal charge.
scenes.shown: In summons cases, Section 274 generally requires the accusation to be stated without a formal charge.

scenes.dialogue: Its proviso requires a reasoned release, with the effect of discharge, if the accusation is groundless.
Special courts and special statutes may have additional rules of their own.
Remember: discharge asks whether the case should proceed. Framing charges identifies what must be answered. Neither is a finding of guilt.
Check the case type, record the correct deadline trigger, and raise your discharge grounds promptly.
If the court moves to frame the charge too early, ask for time, and put your objection on record.
